title: Exterior Painting in Belleview, FL | Block, Stucco, Trim
description: Exterior painting in Belleview, FL for block, stucco, and wood trim. Mildew washed off, cracks sealed, fascia repaired, and up to a 10-year warranty.
h1: Exterior Painting in Belleview, FL, Elevation by Elevation
heroIntro: From the houses around Lake Lillian to the newer streets past downtown, Belleview homes bake in Marion County's afternoon sun and soak in its sticky summers. Our crews clean, fix, and paint every wall according to how hard the weather hits that particular side.

sections.h2: Signs your Belleview exterior is due
body: Run a hand across the south or west wall. If it comes away with a chalky film, the paint has broken down and is no longer shedding water well. Look, too, for paint lifting along the lower lip of the fascia and around door casings, stucco hairlines that have grown wider since last year, and dark green or black streaks wherever the sprinklers hit the wall. Exterior painting in Belleview, FL is about fixing those failures, not just changing the color.
bullets: Peeling at fascia and door-frame edges
Color washed out on the sunniest elevations
Mildew on shaded or sprinkler-wet areas

sections.h2: Coating systems for Belleview's building types
body: Mid-century Belleview homes are often block construction. Block walls have to breathe, so they get a coating that lets vapor out, and every caulk seam where block meets a window frame or wood trim is opened up and redone before the sprayer comes out. Newer homes in the growth area toward The Villages more often have stucco, where hairline cracking is common; we fill those cracks and apply elastomeric coating, which stretches across small movement.

On the wood parts of a Belleview house, trim and fascia are scraped, sanded, primed where bare, then topcoated in 100% acrylic; any board gone soft is swapped for new lumber first. Where a sprayed coat needs to sink in, a painter follows it with a brush or roller. Our guide to stucco cracks explains which cracks paint can handle and which need repair first.

No elevation gets fewer than two complete coats, and a weathered, porous wall or a bold change of color gets three. Your quote names the exact Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore line, which leaves no doubt about which manufacturer warranty applies.

The drier, calmer months from October to May are when Belleview exteriors go smoothest. A summer job is still possible: the crew gets going at daybreak and the lead checks dew point and radar so wet paint never meets a storm. The painting itself usually runs three to seven working days, with washing and dry time on top, and your start date typically lands one to three weeks after you approve. For planning the repaint after this one, read our guide to exterior paint lifespan in Florida.

sections.h2: What you get at the end
body: On the last day, the crew lead circles the whole house with you, and the punch list waits for your signature until each flagged spot is redone. Your Belleview exterior then carries our written workmanship warranty for up to 10 years, stacked on the paint maker's warranty, and the leftover colors are labelled and left in your garage.
Just need the siding cleaned? Book a Belleview house wash. You can also read about our broader exterior painting service or head back to the Belleview overview.

faqs.q: Is elastomeric paint right for my Belleview stucco?
faqs.a: If your stucco shows hairline movement, yes, because elastomeric stretches over those small cracks. Stucco or block that is solid and crack-free is often better served by a top-grade 100% acrylic. The crew lead will recommend one after seeing your walls.

faqs.q: Do you power wash before painting the exterior?
faqs.a: Yes. Each Belleview house is washed and treated for mildew first, and we let it dry fully before any primer or paint goes on.

faqs.q: Can you paint the exterior of my Belleview home in summer?
faqs.a: Yes. Summer crews start at first light and the lead tracks dew point and radar throughout the day, though the October to May stretch is still easier.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted fascia before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Any fascia or trim that is soft gets cut out and replaced, never coated over, and the carpentry is priced on your quote using the photos from the walkthrough.
